# Draft:Russian America for Democracy in Russia

----
Russian America for Democracy in Russia (RADR) is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization established in 2021 to unite pro-democracy Russians across the United States. The organization operates in 18 cities, including Boston, New York, Miami, Chicago, Denver, Sacramento, Los Angeles, and Washington, D.C., with its mission focused on promoting democracy, human rights, and civil liberties in Russia while supporting Russian American communities and opposing authoritarian policies of the Russian government.
Organization's timeline
* January 2021 - started as a network of communities that organized street rallies in response to Alexey Navalny's return to Russian and his arrest.
* November 2021 - RADR registered as a 501(c)(3) charitable organization.
* March 2022 - RADR launched Antipropaganda project.
* October 2022 - RADR launched Freedom Birds for Ukraine.
* November 2022 - Russian parliament proposes to declare RARD and 30 other organizations as undesirable and extremist.
* March 2023 - RADR joined American Coalition for Ukraine for an advocacy campaign in the US Congress.
* October 2023 - Russian authorities blocked Freedom Birds for Ukraine's website in Russia.
* November 2023 - Russian authorities recognized RADR as an undesirable organization (#125 on the list).
* January 2024 - RADR launched Business Navigator project.
* March 2024 - RADR conducted first ever advocacy campaign of pro-democracy Russian American diaspora in the US Congress.
* June 2024 - Freedom Birds for Ukraine raised $250,000 in donations since it launched in 2022.
* September 2024 - RADR joined Ukrainian diaspora organizations for the 5th time to advocate in the US Congress.
* August 2024 - RADR launched Immigration Detention project.
* April 2025 - RADR, in partnership with the Batani Foundation, organized the signing of the Orcas Island Declaration concerning the rights of Indigenous peoples in Russia.
* May 2025 - Russian authorities launched a politically motivated criminal investigation on terrorism-related charges against RADR President Dmitry Valuev and his wife and colleague, Nadia Valueva, who serves as a project coordinator at RADR.
Mission and Projects
RADR is dedicated to strengthening the pro-democracy movement among Russian Americans as well as developing and supporting pro-democracy communities of Russian Americans across the US. It also provides assistance to democratic initiatives in Russia. Since February 2022, the organization has expanded its mission to include fundraising and advocacy efforts in support of Ukraine in response to the ongoing criminal war launched by the Russian government.
Key RADR's projects include:
* Immigration Detention project - providing emergency support to Russian pro-democracy activists and anti-war advocates held in U.S. immigration detention. The project connects detained individuals with pro bono attorneys, supports asylum and habeas corpus litigation, and mobilizes rapid legal action, ensuring that those fleeing political persecution have a fair opportunity to seek protection.
* Adaptation for New Immigrants: RADR conducts activities aiming at helping new Russian immigrants in the US to settle in the new country such as 1) webinars and support groups - RADR hosts webinars and support groups for Russian immigrants in the United States, addressing their everyday needs and challenges, 2) Business Navigator – educational program for new immigrants about how to start and conduct business in the US.
* Street protests, pickets, memorial events: RADR organizes street rallies in support, and then in memory of Alexey Navalny and other political prisoners, since February 2022 – in support of Ukraine amid the brutal Russian aggression against Ukraine. RADR communities hold memorial events to commemorate victims of political persecution in Russia as a part of Returning the names campaign by Memorial. Since the beginning of the full-scale invasion of Ukraine, RADR activists from the Sacramento community have been joining Ukrainians at the California State Capitol on the 24th of each month for rallies in support of Ukraine.
* Advocacy and Awareness: Organizing events, advocacy campaigns - including those conducted in cooperation with Ukrainian organizations - and briefings for U.S. decision-makers on human rights violations in Russia, the destructive influence of Vladimir Putin's dictatorship both in the United States and globally, and the efforts of Russian resistance movements inside the country and throughout the diaspora.
* Support for Political Prisoners: Conducting letter-writing campaigns to political prisoners in Russia, as well as raising funds to support isolated and lesser-known political prisoners and Ukrainians held in Russian prisons.
* Research Initiatives: 1) property research - the organization conducts research on properties in the United States owned by Russian government officials, Putin's associates, and key figures of the Russian ruling class, 2) pro-Kremlin organizations research - RADR conducts research of pro-Kremlin organization and individuals in the United States that act on behalf or in favor of Russian government and in support of Putin's policies.
* Freedom Birds for Ukraine: RADR initiated the "Freedom Birds for Ukraine" crowdfunding project to provide support to Ukrainians affected by the full-scale invasion, offering both humanitarian aid and essential resources. In 2025 FBU became a separate nonprofit entity.
* Social Media Campaigns (Antipropaganda): Disseminating factual information about the war in Ukraine through Russian-language platforms to counter misinformation and censorship.
Global Connections
RADR is part of a global network of pro-democracy and anti-war Russian diaspora organizations, including Free Russian Global, the Anti-War Committee of Russia and the Antiwar Initiatives Platform. This network spans continents, fostering collaboration among Russian expatriates to promote freedom, democracy, and human rights worldwide.

Meetings with prominent Russian opposition leaders
RADR has organized and helped to organize community meetings for prominent Russian opposition figures who met with local Russian communities across the United States.
* 2021 - Leonid Volkov and Maria Pevchikh (New York)
* 2022 - Leonid Volkov (Sacramento, Los Angeles), Vladimir Milov (Miami), Sergey Aleksashenko (Washington, DC), Lyubov Sobol (Washington, DC)
* 2023 - Leonid Volkov (Denver, San Francisco, Washington, DC), Mikhail Khodorkovsky (New York, Washington, DC), Maria Pevchikh (Washington, DC, New York), Ivan Zhdanov (Miami)
* 2024 - Sister Vassa (Larina) and Sergey Chapnin (Chicago), Sergey Aleksashenko (Chicago), Anastasia Shevchenko and Dmitry Gudkov (Washington, DC), Ekaterina Shulman and Maxim Kurnikov
* 2025 - Tamara Eidelman (New York, Washington, DC, Chicago)
and Anastasia Shevchenko meet with pro-democracy Russian American diaspora in Washington, DC]]
Impact
RADR's impact lies in transforming Russian American communities into active forces for change: raising hundreds of thousands in aid, supporting Russian immigrants through adaptation and legal aid, exposing the Kremlin's influence networks, and sustaining hope for democracy in Russia. Its work has been recognized in broader analyses of Russian anti-war resistance, positioning it as a key player in diaspora-led opposition.
